item.description:
ALC section (/alc/) ¶

This directory implements the Apache Local Community (ALC) section of the ComDev website: a landing page with an interactive map of chapters, a single chapters page that lists every chapter inline, a “start a chapter” guide, and an organizer guide. Each chapter is one Markdown data file, but by default no standalone page is generated for it (see “Chapter page model” below).

What each file is ¶

source/alc/
├── _index.md             Landing page. Intro, embedded map + chapter
│                         list (via shortcodes), how to get involved,
│                         contact. URL: /alc/
├── start-a-chapter.md     How to establish a chapter + the program rules
│                         (one-per-city, metro exceptions, CoC, quarterly
│                         reports, 3-month inactivity dissolution, no
│                         press releases). Includes the front-matter
│                         template for adding a chapter.
├── organizers.md          Practical guide for chapter organizers (running
│                         events, finding speakers, reporting, resources).
└── chapters/
    ├── _index.md          Chapter list page. URL: /alc/chapters/
    └── <city>.md          One file per chapter (the data model). Front
                           matter drives the map + list; body is the blurb
                           shown inline on the chapters page. Headless by
                           default — no standalone page (see below).

item.title: ALC Organizer Guide
item.description:
ALC organizer guide ¶

Running an ALC chapter is mostly about showing up consistently for your local open source community. This page collects practical help for chapter organizers.

  • Running events
  • Finding speakers
  • Topic ideas
  • Reporting
  • Resources

Running events ¶

The heart of a chapter is its events. These don’t need to be large or elaborate — a regular, reliable, welcoming meetup does far more for a community than an occasional big conference.

  • Start small and regular. A predictable monthly or quarterly cadence builds an audience.
  • Mix formats: talks, workshops, hack sessions, and informal socials all have their place.
  • Welcome newcomers explicitly. Many attendees will be students or people entirely new to open source.

Finding speakers ¶

You don’t have to find every speaker yourself.

item.description:
Info: Daniel Ruggeri shared some great ideas on ALC Outreach activities for educational institutes on the ComDev mailing list.
Here is the reference to mail thread https://s.apache.org/683ol

Important - We are documenting here (in raw format) for reference purposes so that we don’t miss this information in the future.
As we established some more ALCs, we will make a more detailed execution plan on these ideas.

Notes from the mail, quoting Daniel Ruggeri:

item.title: Apache Local Community - ALC
item.description:
This wiki is used for Apache Local Community (ALC).

About ALC ¶

ALC comprises local groups of Apache (Open Source) enthusiasts, called an ‘ALC Chapter’.
There will be a single ALC chapter per town/city.

ALC is similar to Google Developer Group, Facebook Developer Circles, Mozilla Reps.

Info: For metropolitan geographic areas (like San Francisco Bay Area and Los Angeles etc.), multiple ALC Chapters can be setup.
ComDev PMC will look into the requests from these areas and took the decision on case-by-case basis.

item.title: Guidelines to manage an ALC Chapter
item.description:
Adding a new member to ALC Chapter ¶

The ALC Chapter is responsible for adding new members to that ALC Chapters.

If the interested person is an ASF Committer, PMC member, or ASF Member, they can be directly added to the ALC chapter. In this case, simply send an update email to the private list at private@community.apache.org informing them about the new addition.

However, if the interested volunteer is not an ASF Committer, PMC member, or ASF Member, an existing chapter member should initiate an internal vote among the current chapter members. This vote email should include private@community.apache.org in CC.

item.title: Process to dissolve an ALC Chapter
item.description:
If an ALC Chapter is inactive for 3 months (or any reason including lack of reporting, no longer having required guidance, event branding issues, etc.), it will be dissolved after communication with the ALC chapter members because we are having strictly one ALC chapter in a town/city.

1. The ALC Chair will make sure quarterly report is filed by ALC Chapter.

2. In case of failure of filing the report, the ALC Chair will have communication with ALC chapter members (by keeping ComDev PMC in the loop) to understand the actual situation.

item.title: Process to establish an ALC Chapter
item.description:
The following process will be followed to establish an ALC Chapter. Step 1: ¶

1. A volunteer will request to establish an ALC Chapter by sending a message to dev@community.apache.org with “[ALC] Request to establish ALC in <name-of-your-town-or-city>” in the subject line.
Before sending the request, the volunteer needs to make sure the following points are addressed

1.1 There will be a single ALC chapter per town/city, so before sending the request please check the ALC Chapters to see if there’s an existing chapter in your location.

item.title: Roles and Responsibilities in managing ALC initiative
item.description:
ALC Chair ¶

The ALC Chair will be responsible for ensuring:

  1. The quarterly report is filed by all the ALC Chapters.
  2. Pre-event materials are reviewed with the help of PMC.
  3. ComDev PMC will reach out to ALC Chair for $reasons.

ALC Chapter Lead ¶

Each ALC Chapter will have one Chapter Lead and will have the following roles and responsibilities.

  1. Making sure the ALC Code of Conduct is followed by their ALC Chapter.
  2. All the events organized by the ALC Chapter are following the Guidelines to organise ALC Event.
  3. Submit the status report to ComDev (mailto:dev@community.apache.org) in every three months based on their reporting cycle.
    (keep your other ALC Chapter members in CC.)
  4. The Chapter activities are in line with ALC Roles and Responsibilities.
  5. Chapter Lead will be the point of contact for the respective ALC Chapter.

ALC Chapter Member ¶

  1. Making sure the ALC Code of Conduct is followed by ALC Chapter.
  2. Making sure all the events organized by the ALC Chapter are following the Guidelines to organise ALC Event.
  3. Contribute to activities that are in line with ALC Roles and Responsibilities.
  4. Help in preparing the status report to ComDev in every three months based on their reporting cycle.
  5. As the Chapter Members have edit rights to Confluence, keep updated all the information available in the Chapter’s space, like Reports, respective events detail pages.
  6. Maintain the ALC Resources document.

item.title: Start an ALC Chapter
item.description:
Start an ALC chapter ¶

So there’s no ALC chapter in your town or city yet, and you’d like to start one. Wonderful! Here’s what’s involved.

  • Before you apply
  • How to apply
  • Adding your chapter to this site

Before you apply ¶

  • Check the map first. There is a single ALC chapter per town or city. Look at the list of chapters to make sure one doesn’t already exist in your location.
  • For large metropolitan areas (for example, the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, or Mumbai), more than one chapter can make sense. The ComDev PMC reviews these requests and decides on a case-by-case basis.

How to apply ¶

The formal application steps are maintained on the ALC wiki, in the Process to establish an ALC Chapter document, linked from the ALC program page. In outline:
